ForPropertyManagers.faqTitle: Frequently asked questions for property management firms

faq.question: Do you invoice per building, or one single invoice for my whole portfolio?
faq.answer: Each community gets its own invoice, itemising the services it has contracted, even though you manage several buildings with us. That way every residents' association sees exactly what its own community pays, without it being mixed with the rest of your portfolio.

faq.question: Do I need a separate contract for each community?
faq.answer: Yes, each community signs its own service contract (they're separate legal entities), but you keep the same point of contact and the same service standard across every building you manage with us, so adding a new one doesn't mean renegotiating from scratch.

faq.question: If an issue affects several communities in my portfolio, who do I contact?
faq.answer: Your usual contact at Imora: there's no need to report separately to a different concierge, cleaning company and technician at each building. A single team coordinates the response even though the communities are legally independent.

faq.question: Can I add a new building without renegotiating the terms of the others?
faq.answer: Yes, each new building is quoted based on the services that specific community needs, but we apply the same reporting process and the same service standard you already know from the rest of your portfolio, without having to re-explain how you work.

faq.question: What if a community in my portfolio already has a service contracted with another provider?
faq.answer: We can step in only for the services the community decides to outsource to us, and coordinate the handover with the outgoing provider so there's no coverage gap during the switch.

faq.question: Do I get a single report covering all my communities, or do I need to check building by building?
faq.answer: Your contact at Imora knows the status of every community in your portfolio, so you can ask for a combined view instead of having to ask service by service and building by building.

faq.question: Does the inspection team visit all my buildings, or only the ones with problems?
faq.answer: We visit every community with contracted services, not only the ones that have had an incident, precisely to catch a problem before it reaches the residents' meeting.

faq.question: How do you put together a proposal if I manage many communities at once?
faq.answer: We prepare a proposal per building, detailing which services each one already has contracted and which could be outsourced to Imora, so you can bring it to each residents' meeting separately if you need to.

madrid.name: Madrid
madrid.heroSubtitle: 24-hour concierge cover, security and maintenance for communities, offices and shopping centres across Madrid city's 21 districts.
madrid.context: Madrid city brings together 21 very different districts: from the dense residential blocks over 60 years old in Centro, Chamberí or Tetuán, to the office towers of the central business area and the newer developments in districts such as Vicálvaro or Villa de Vallecas. That diversity means the same provider has to handle a traditional entrance hall with long-standing residents and a corporate headquarters with electronic access control in the same neighbourhood.

faq.question: Do you work across every district of Madrid city, including those further from the centre?
faq.answer: Yes, we cover all 21 districts; the team assigned to each community or building is organised according to its exact location, from Centro to districts such as Vicálvaro or Villaverde.

faq.question: Can you cover an office building in the central business district as well as a residential community?
faq.answer: Yes, the same services (concierge, cleaning, maintenance, security) apply equally to company premises, residential communities and shopping centres, in any district.

faq.question: How do you run the service in a city-centre building with no loading bay or vehicle access?
faq.answer: With materials and equipment sized to come in through the front door, and hours agreed with the community so as not to clash with residents coming and going. Inside the M-30 that is the norm: the work is done first thing, with hand trolleys, not from a van parked at the façade.

serviceNotes.concierge: In districts with more office buildings, concierge cover tends to span long reception and access-control shifts; in the more residential neighbourhoods of Centro or Chamberí, the concierge remains the familiar point of contact for long-standing residents.
serviceNotes.security: The business districts of the central area tend to combine concierge cover with video surveillance and electronic access control, especially overnight and at weekends, less common in purely residential neighbourhoods.
serviceNotes.pools: Communal pools are more common in peripheral districts with more space per community, such as Hortaleza or Fuencarral-El Pardo, than in the dense blocks of Centro, but both require a qualified lifeguard during the season.
serviceNotes.cleaning: In the buildings over 60 years old in Centro, Chamberí or Tetuán, the entrance, stairs and lift see far more daily traffic than in a peripheral district, so cleaning frequency tends to be higher.
serviceNotes.gardening: Interior courtyards and communal gardens are common in districts with larger blocks, such as Chamartín or Salamanca, while in historic Centro a building's own green space is the exception rather than the rule.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Coordinating plumbing, electrics and locksmithing with a single provider means a community in Centro over 60 years old doesn't need to call a different technician for every fault.

pozuelo-de-alarcon.name: Pozuelo de Alarcón
pozuelo-de-alarcon.heroSubtitle: Pool maintenance and gardening for the Somosaguas developments and the rest of Pozuelo de Alarcón, 14 km from Madrid.
pozuelo-de-alarcon.context: Along with Boadilla, Pozuelo de Alarcón has the highest average declared income in the Community of Madrid, with developments like Somosaguas sitting alongside high-rise residential towers near the Casa de Campo park. That mix means a single portfolio of communities can include a detached house with its own pool and a tower with a concierge and several shared pools.

faq.question: Do you cover both Somosaguas and the high-rise areas of Pozuelo?
faq.answer: Yes, the same range of services adapts to the type of property: from a plot with its own pool in Somosaguas to a residential tower with several communal pools.

faq.question: Does gardening cover large green areas, like those in a housing development?
faq.answer: Yes, we adapt the team and frequency to the actual size of the green area, from a house garden to the shared grounds of an entire development.

faq.question: Can you run a detached-housing development and a residential tower block at the same time?
faq.answer: Yes, and in Pozuelo the two sit close together. They are different plans: the development needs internal roads, gardens and access control across several entrances, while the tower needs the entrance hall, lifts and garage. The point of contact is the same; the proposal is not.

serviceNotes.concierge: In the high-rise residential towers near the Casa de Campo, concierge cover usually combines access control for several entrances under one community, unlike the individual houses of Somosaguas.
serviceNotes.security: In the Somosaguas housing areas, security focuses on access control and perimeter surveillance for the plot, while in high-rise towers it integrates with the building's concierge service.
serviceNotes.pools: Pozuelo has a high number of private and communal pools per community, as you would expect in a town of developments. We handle the chemical maintenance, the cleaning, and opening and closing the season for each pool.
serviceNotes.cleaning: In high-rise residential towers, cleaning covers several entrances and lifts under one community, while in the house developments it focuses on shared access points and communal areas.
serviceNotes.gardening: A private garden per plot is common in Somosaguas, while in high-rise towers green areas are managed as shared space across several entrances.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Between the Somosaguas plots and the high-rise residential towers, technical maintenance in Pozuelo covers everything from individual house installations to shared areas in multi-entrance communities.

alcorcon.name: Alcorcón
alcorcon.heroSubtitle: Technical maintenance and cleaning for the communities of Alcorcón, a former industrial town 14 km from Madrid.
alcorcon.context: Alcorcón grew rapidly between the 1960s and 1990s around one of the oldest industrial estates in southern Madrid, leaving behind a stock of medium and large block communities with several decades of use. In that type of building, installations (plumbing, electrics, entry phones) are starting to need renovations that a more recently built property doesn't require yet.

faq.question: Can you handle maintenance for a building from the 1970s or 80s in Alcorcón?
faq.answer: Yes, our own technical team handles plumbing, electrical and locksmith faults in buildings of any age, including the renovations the municipality's older installations are starting to need.

faq.question: Does cleaning include garages and outdoor areas?
faq.answer: Yes, the cleaning plan covers the entrance, stairs, garage and shared outdoor areas, at the frequency each community decides.

faq.question: What do you check first in a 1970s or 1980s block in Alcorcón?
faq.answer: Downpipes, roof and the main electrical panel. In the blocks that grew alongside the industrial estate, those three are what have gone longest untouched and what generate the most call-outs later. The first preventive visit focuses there before proposing anything else.

serviceNotes.concierge: In Alcorcón's medium and large block communities, mostly built during the industrial growth of the 1960s to 90s, concierge services tend to focus on access control and attending residents in the morning and afternoon.
serviceNotes.security: Electronic access control is gaining ground in Alcorcón's older buildings that are renewing their original entry phone system, as a complement to traditional concierge cover.
serviceNotes.pools: In the medium-sized blocks built during Alcorcón's industrial growth, the pool often shares its maintenance budget with communal areas, so it's worth coordinating both with the same provider.
serviceNotes.cleaning: Alcorcón has a good number of medium and large blocks with several decades of daily use behind them. In communal areas with that kind of wear we match the cleaning frequency to each entrance's actual footfall, rather than applying the same routine across the whole building.
serviceNotes.gardening: In the blocks built during the municipality's industrial growth, green areas tend to be smaller than in a housing development, but still need regular upkeep.
serviceNotes.maintenance: The plumbing, electrical and entry-phone installations of buildings from the 1960s to the 90s are starting to need periodic renewal. In Alcorcón, where the housing stock grew alongside the industrial estate, maintenance is usually framed as a phased plan rather than as isolated faults.

majadahonda.name: Majadahonda
majadahonda.heroSubtitle: Security and access control for the gated developments of Majadahonda, 17 km north-west of Madrid.
majadahonda.context: Majadahonda has one of the highest shares of single-family housing in north-western Madrid, with gated developments surrounding a town centre whose shopping streets get busy at weekends. Since most properties are developments with several access points and internal roads, controlling who comes and goes weighs more heavily on service demand than in a conventional block-housing municipality.

faq.question: Do you install access control in gated developments with several internal roads?
faq.answer: Yes, we design the system around the development's actual access points, with cards or codes the community can assign per household, covering pedestrian and vehicle entrances separately.

faq.question: Can you manage several different developments in the same area?
faq.answer: Yes, if your firm manages several communities in Majadahonda or nearby, take a look at our services for property managers too.

faq.question: How do you cover a gated development with several entrances and its own internal roads?
faq.answer: With access control at each entrance and a concierge patrol along the internal roads, rather than a fixed post at a single gate. Most developments in Majadahonda have more than one way in, and covering only the main one leaves the rest unattended.

serviceNotes.concierge: In Majadahonda's gated developments, with several internal roads, concierge services tend to combine with general access control for the development, rather than a single entrance.
serviceNotes.security: With one of the highest shares of single-family housing in north-western Madrid, security and access control for gated developments weigh more heavily on demand in Majadahonda than in a conventional block-housing municipality.
serviceNotes.pools: Many of Majadahonda's developments have a communal pool. We handle the chemical maintenance and cleaning throughout the season, and provide a qualified lifeguard where the pool's capacity requires one.
serviceNotes.cleaning: Beyond the communal areas of block communities, in gated developments with several internal roads cleaning tends to extend to shared pedestrian and vehicle access points.
serviceNotes.gardening: Majadahonda's gated developments have their own landscaped areas and green roads. We maintain them with scheduled visits, and can fold the communal pool into the same plan.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Without an entrance hall or lift like an urban block, technical maintenance in Majadahonda focuses on perimeter fencing, internal roads and the development's own installations.

las-rozas.name: Las Rozas de Madrid
las-rozas.heroSubtitle: Video surveillance and security for the developments and the retail and tech hub of Las Rozas, 20 km from Madrid.
las-rozas.context: Las Rozas combines large residential developments with a significant retail and office presence, with large shopping centres and business parks that draw traffic from outside the municipality on weekends and during working hours. That external footfall gives video surveillance and access control a different weight than in a purely residential municipality, both in the developments and in communities near those commercial areas.

faq.question: Do you cover both residential developments and communities near the shopping areas of Las Rozas?
faq.answer: Yes, the same range of services adapts to the type of property: from a development with several internal streets to a block community near the municipality's shopping areas.

faq.question: What does video surveillance cover for a large development?
faq.answer: We design the system around the development's actual access points (entrances, garages, communal areas) and handle quarterly maintenance of cameras and recorders.

faq.question: Do you also serve business parks and retail units, not just residential communities?
faq.answer: Yes. In Las Rozas we work both residential communities and offices and retail units, with the difference that in the retail setting the extra cleaning and concierge cover is concentrated at weekends, when the out-of-town footfall arrives.

serviceNotes.concierge: In block communities near the retail and office hub of Las Rozas, concierge services follow a more traditional entrance-hall format, while in the larger developments it combines with general access control.
serviceNotes.security: With a retail and office presence that draws traffic from outside the municipality, security and video surveillance carry a different weight in Las Rozas than in a purely residential municipality, both in developments and in communities near those areas.
serviceNotes.pools: Communities in Las Rozas with a pool, whether in a block or a development, need a qualified lifeguard and chemical maintenance throughout the bathing season under current regulations.
serviceNotes.cleaning: In block communities near the municipality's retail and office hub, cleaning of communal areas is requested at a frequency similar to any established urban community.
serviceNotes.gardening: The larger developments in Las Rozas have considerably more shared landscaped surface than a community near the retail hub, so the gardening plan and the visit frequency are set separately in each case.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Between the larger developments and the block communities near the retail and office hub, technical maintenance in Las Rozas covers very different profiles within the same municipality.

boadilla-del-monte.name: Boadilla del Monte
boadilla-del-monte.heroSubtitle: Pool and garden care for the terraced-house communities of Boadilla del Monte, 19 km west of Madrid.
boadilla-del-monte.context: Boadilla del Monte, one of the municipalities with the highest average income in the region, has an almost entirely low-density layout of terraced houses grouped into small communities, with very little of the vertical block housing typical of other towns in the metropolitan area. These small communities usually share landscaped areas and a pool from the moment they're set up.

faq.question: Do you work with small communities of terraced houses, with few homes?
faq.answer: Yes, we adapt the maintenance and cleaning plan to the community's actual size, with no minimum number of homes required, common in Boadilla's low-density layout.

faq.question: Can I contract only gardening and pool care, without the other services?
faq.answer: Yes, each service is contracted independently based on what the community already has covered.

faq.question: Is it worth hiring services if the community is only ten or twelve houses?
faq.answer: Yes, and in Boadilla that is the most common size. For small communities we adjust the frequency rather than assign permanent staff: fortnightly gardening, weekly cleaning of communal areas and monthly preventive maintenance work out at a manageable cost per home.

serviceNotes.concierge: In Boadilla's small terraced-house communities, concierge services usually combine with access control for the whole development, not a single home.
serviceNotes.security: In a municipality with an almost total predominance of low-density developments, access control in Boadilla covers a wide perimeter rather than a single entrance, unlike towns with more vertical block housing.
serviceNotes.pools: There is little vertical block housing in Boadilla: what predominates are small communities that have shared a pool since they were set up. We handle the chemical maintenance, the cleaning, and opening and closing the season.
serviceNotes.cleaning: In Boadilla's low-density developments, cleaning of communal areas focuses less on entrance halls and more on shared access points, the pool and collective-use areas of small communities.
serviceNotes.gardening: In Boadilla's terraced-house communities, landscaped communal areas are the norm, not the exception. We maintain them at whatever frequency each garden calls for, and can take on the pool as well.
serviceNotes.maintenance: With several terraced houses sharing the same pool installation or access point in small communities, a single technical fault in Boadilla can affect the whole community rather than one isolated home.

alcobendas.name: Alcobendas
alcobendas.heroSubtitle: Concierge and security for the offices of the Chaparral business park and the communities of Alcobendas, 15 km from Madrid.
alcobendas.context: Alcobendas hosts one of the largest business parks in the Community of Madrid, with major company headquarters alongside medium-to-high-rise residential communities. That mix makes Alcobendas one of the few towns in the metropolitan area where concierge and security services for corporate premises generate as much demand as services for residential communities.

faq.question: Do you cover offices and business parks, not just residential communities?
faq.answer: Yes, concierge, security and cleaning are contracted the same way for business-park offices as for residential communities.

faq.question: Can you cover several buildings of the same company in Alcobendas?
faq.answer: Yes, a single point of contact can coordinate service across several premises or buildings of the same company within the municipality.

faq.question: Can you maintain a company's headquarters and the residential communities next door at once?
faq.answer: Yes. Alcobendas has one of the region's largest business parks right up against block-housing neighbourhoods, and running both on the same route brings travel costs down. The contracts stay separate, with different hours and service levels.

serviceNotes.concierge: With one of the region's largest business parks in Alcobendas, concierge services for company premises see demand as constant as that from the municipality's residential communities.
serviceNotes.security: Alcobendas puts one of the region's largest business parks next to medium-to-high-rise residential communities. We provide video surveillance and access control in both settings, as separate projects: at a company's premises it is hours and external staff that drive the design; in a community, the entrances and the garage.
serviceNotes.pools: In Alcobendas' medium-to-high-rise residential communities, pool maintenance follows the usual seasonal calendar, with a qualified lifeguard.
serviceNotes.cleaning: Both the business park's corporate premises and Alcobendas' medium-to-high-rise residential communities request ongoing cleaning, though with different needs depending on whether it's an office or a residential communal area.
serviceNotes.gardening: Maintenance of green areas in Alcobendas is split between the residential block communities and the outdoor spaces of the municipality's corporate premises.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Technical maintenance in Alcobendas covers both office installations, given the weight of its business park, and callouts from medium-to-high-rise residential communities.

san-sebastian-de-los-reyes.name: San Sebastián de los Reyes
san-sebastian-de-los-reyes.heroSubtitle: Gardening and communal area maintenance for the new developments of San Sebastián de los Reyes, 20 km north of Madrid.
san-sebastian-de-los-reyes.context: San Sebastián de los Reyes has seen intense urban growth over the last two decades, with new residential neighbourhoods that have more than doubled its population since the 1990s, alongside a more established town centre with traditional block communities. The developments from that recent expansion usually include landscaped areas and a pool from year one, while the historic centre retains a housing stock from another era.

faq.question: Do you maintain recently built communities in the newer parts of the municipality?
faq.answer: Yes, our technical team covers both the older town centre and the more recent expansion developments, with the same fast-response approach to faults.

faq.question: How often can gardening be contracted in the newer parts of the municipality?
faq.answer: Whatever each community decides: from fortnightly upkeep to weekly visits, depending on the size of the green area.

faq.question: Does maintenance differ between the new neighbourhoods and the old centre of San Sebastián de los Reyes?
faq.answer: Quite a lot. In the developments of the last two decades the work goes into garages, large communal areas and irrigation systems; in the established centre it goes into downpipes, entrance halls and joinery. We assess it on the visit rather than applying the same plan to both.

serviceNotes.concierge: In San Sebastián de los Reyes' new developments, concierge services are usually coordinated from the community's first year, while in the older town centre it works alongside an already established entrance hall.
serviceNotes.security: Electronic access control is standard from the outset in developments from the municipality's most recent expansion, unlike the established town centre, where it's usually added later.
serviceNotes.pools: Communities with a pool in the municipality, both in the new developments and the more established centre, need chemical maintenance and a qualified lifeguard throughout the bathing season.
serviceNotes.cleaning: Cleaning of communal areas in San Sebastián de los Reyes is split between the traditional town centre and the new residential neighbourhoods that have more than doubled the municipality's population since the 1990s.
serviceNotes.gardening: With urban growth that has more than doubled the population since the 1990s, San Sebastián de los Reyes' new developments usually include landscaped areas from year one, more so than the historic centre.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Maintenance of communal areas covers both the developments from the most recent expansion and the traditional block communities of San Sebastián de los Reyes' established town centre.

tres-cantos.name: Tres Cantos
tres-cantos.heroSubtitle: Gardening and green area maintenance in Tres Cantos, a low-density planned town 24 km north of Madrid.
tres-cantos.context: Tres Cantos was built from scratch as a planned town in the 1970s, with a low-density layout, plenty of open space between blocks and protected natural land across much of its area. With so much shared green space built into the design, garden maintenance tends to weigh more heavily on a Tres Cantos community's budget than in a conventional urban block elsewhere in the metropolitan area.

faq.question: Does the gardening service include automatic irrigation for communal areas?
faq.answer: Yes, we check and programme automatic irrigation systems to adjust water use to the season.

faq.question: Can you handle a community with several separate green areas?
faq.answer: Yes, we adapt the team and frequency to the actual size of the green areas, whether there's one or several within the same community.

faq.question: How do you maintain so much green space between blocks without the cost running away?
faq.answer: By grouping mowing and pruning into longer, less frequent visits, and checking the irrigation before summer so no water is wasted. Tres Cantos was planned with a lot of open space between buildings, and gardening weighs more here than in a block between party walls.

serviceNotes.concierge: In Tres Cantos' communities, designed from the outset with extensive landscaped areas, concierge services usually coordinate with the maintenance of those shared green spaces.
serviceNotes.security: Access control in Tres Cantos' communities adapts to a planned layout with more open space between blocks than in a municipality that grew without planning.

serviceNotes.concierge: In Fuenlabrada's extensive stock of medium and large residential blocks, mostly built during the rapid growth of the 1970s to 90s, concierge services usually combine with ongoing technical maintenance from the same team.

serviceNotes.concierge: Móstoles is the most populous town in the region after Madrid city, with an enormous stock of residential communities. We provide concierge cover on 6 to 24-hour shifts, matched to the size and entrance footfall of each property.
serviceNotes.security: Access control is gaining ground in Móstoles' larger blocks, as a complement to concierge services in buildings where a single control point doesn't cover every access.

torrejon-de-ardoz.name: Torrejón de Ardoz

faq.question: How does traffic from the industrial estates affect Coslada's residential communities?

serviceNotes.concierge: In Coslada's medium-sized blocks, well-adjusted concierge hours make more of a difference than in a small building, where physical presence matters less day to day.
serviceNotes.security: With one of southern Europe's largest rail logistics hubs within its boundaries, security and access control see a different level of demand in Coslada than in a purely residential town in the eastern metropolitan area.

rivas-vaciamadrid.name: Rivas-Vaciamadrid

serviceNotes.concierge: In Rivas-Vaciamadrid's planned developments, concierge services are usually coordinated from the community's first year, alongside the rest of the services for the already built installations.

serviceNotes.maintenance: Technical maintenance in Rivas-Vaciamadrid is needed from the community's formation, since the installations of its developments, almost all post-1990s, are new alongside the rest of the services.

colmenar-viejo.name: Colmenar Viejo
colmenar-viejo.heroSubtitle: Gardening and maintenance for the historic centre and outlying developments of Colmenar Viejo, next to open grazing land, 29 km north of Madrid.
colmenar-viejo.context: Colmenar Viejo keeps a historic centre with a cattle-farming tradition surrounded by open grazing land and hillside, with streets of low-rise stairwell buildings, alongside more recently built developments on its outskirts with more single-family housing and landscaped areas. serviceNotes.maintenance: Technical maintenance in Colmenar Viejo covers both low-rise stairwell buildings in the historic centre and communities in the outlying developments, each with different needs.

serviceNotes.cleaning: In Torrelodones' developments, cleaning focuses more on shared access points and communal areas than individual block entrance halls, uncommon in this municipality.
serviceNotes.gardening: The single-family developments of Torrelodones, at the foot of the Guadarrama mountains, have their own gardens and green areas. We maintain them on a schedule adjusted to the mountain climate.
serviceNotes.maintenance: Technical maintenance in Torrelodones covers the communal installations of the single-family housing developments spread between the town centre and the slopes towards the mountains.

collado-villalba.name: Collado Villalba

overview.question: What services does Imora offer?
overview.answer: Concierge and access control, video surveillance and access control, pool maintenance, cleaning and gardening, and building maintenance. The permanent staff on these services is mostly hired directly.

concierge.question: What does the concierge service include?
concierge.answer: Reception, access control, mail distribution and resident assistance, with flexible hours from 6 to 24 hours depending on each building's needs.

security.question: How does the security and CCTV service work?
security.answer: We handle the project, installation and maintenance of video surveillance and access control systems, protecting your building or shopping centre end to end.

maintenance.question: Do you handle building maintenance?
maintenance.answer: Yes. Our own technical team covers plumbing, electrics, locksmithing and small works in common areas, with a fast response to faults.

coverage.question: Which areas do you work in?
coverage.answer: We serve businesses, homeowner communities, buildings, shopping centres and car parks in Madrid capital and 19 more municipalities across its metropolitan area (northwest, north, south and east belts). You can check the full list on our coverage areas page.

schedule.question: What concierge hours can I contract?
schedule.answer: Whatever your building needs: from 6 to 24 hours of service. We adapt the schedule to each community's reality, not the other way round.

availability.question: Do you offer support outside office hours?
availability.answer: Yes. In addition to office hours, we run an incident hotline answered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, for anything that can't wait. It is phone support and coordination of the response: on-site presence is whatever hours you have contracted.

quote.question: How do I request a quote?
quote.answer: Fill in the contact form or call us directly. We carry out an on-site visit and assessment of your community or building, and prepare a fixed quote with a reply within 48 hours, with no obligation.

changeService.question: I want to extend or change my contracted service, who do I talk to?
changeService.answer: Our sales team, who will review your new needs with you and prepare an updated proposal. You can write to them directly from the contact page.

substitutions.question: What happens if a concierge or technician is absent or on leave?
substitutions.answer: We cover any absence with a guaranteed substitute at no extra cost, so the service is never interrupted.

quality.question: How do you monitor service quality?
quality.answer: Our inspection department visits every service on site on a regular basis, to check that what was agreed is being delivered and to spot improvements before they become incidents.

existingClient.question: I'm already an Imora client, where do I get support?

concierge.title: Concierge and access control
concierge.summary: Reception, access control, mail handling and support for residents, staff or customers, with flexible schedules from 6 to 24 hours for communities, buildings, businesses and shopping centres.
concierge.description: A concierge is the first impression of your community, your building or your business, and the filter that keeps unauthorised people out. We select and train our own staff for residential lobbies, company premises and shopping-centre entrances, and cover sick leave and holidays without ever leaving the desk empty.
concierge.cta: Request concierge for my community, building or business

subservices.title: Reception and resident support
subservices.description: The concierge works to recognise residents and to know which suppliers each home has authorised: the more stable the post, the sooner that happens. Anything they cannot solve on the spot is logged in a daily report that reaches the property manager the same day, not at the end of the month.

subservices.title: Access control
subservices.description: Every visit is logged with its entry time, and the concierge checks the identity of anyone they do not recognise before letting them through. Couriers and delivery drivers follow a specific protocol so residents are not disturbed at night. The log is kept following the community's instructions and data protection law: only what is necessary is recorded, it is kept for the agreed period and it is not used for anything else.

subservices.title: Mail and parcels
subservices.description: Parcels requiring a signature are stored in an identified space and the resident is notified through whichever channel the community chooses: a physical note, WhatsApp or an app. Registered mail and official notices are handled with proof of receipt, and only where the community has authorised in writing that the concierge may receive them on residents' behalf.

subservices.title: Cover for sick leave and holidays
subservices.description: Before starting their shift, the substitute is briefed on the building's particulars: residents with special needs, regular suppliers, open incidents. The goal is for the change of person to go unnoticed by the community.

faq.question: How much does the concierge service cost?
faq.answer: It depends on the coverage hours (part-time or 24 hours) and the size of the building. We prepare a fixed quote after visiting the property, with no hidden fees.

faq.question: Can I switch concierge providers without issues?
faq.answer: Yes. We handle the transition with the current property administrator, and if the existing concierge wants to stay on, we consider bringing them onto Imora's team.

faq.question: What happens if the concierge gets sick?
faq.answer: We cover the absence with another professional of the same profile, at no extra cost and with no interruption to the service.

faq.question: Can I hire coverage for mornings only?
faq.answer: Yes, shifts are adapted to what each community needs: half-day, split shift or full 6-to-24-hour coverage.

faq.question: How are visitors and delivery drivers logged?
faq.answer: The concierge verifies the identity of anyone they do not recognise and notes the time of entry. Delivery drivers and couriers follow a specific protocol so residents are not disturbed outside agreed hours.

faq.question: What happens to parcels that arrive when nobody is home?
faq.answer: They are kept in a designated space in the entrance hall and the resident is notified through whichever channel the community chooses: a paper note, WhatsApp or an app. Registered mail always requires a signature.

faq.question: Can concierge services be hired for an office building, not just a residential community?
faq.answer: Yes. The service adapts equally to homeowner communities, company headquarters and shopping centre entrances, with the same criteria for selecting and training staff.

faq.question: How does the handover work if we already have a concierge we want to keep?
faq.answer: We manage the transition with your current property manager, and if the concierge wants to stay in the building, we look at bringing them onto the Imora team rather than replacing them.

faq.question: What visitor data is kept, and what happens to it?
faq.answer: Only what is needed to know who came in and when: usually name, reason for the visit, destination home and time. The data controller is the community; we keep the log on their behalf, under their instructions and a data processing agreement. It is not shared with third parties, it is not used for anything other than access control, and it is kept for the period the community has set.

communities.title: Homeowner communities
communities.description: The concierge knows the residents and their recurring issues, so they resolve directly what an outsider would have to ask about first: who holds the key to which storage unit, when the cleaning team comes by, or which resident reported a leak.

propertyManagers.title: Property management firms
propertyManagers.description: A single concierge team can cover several buildings in your portfolio with the same criteria for hours, incident reporting and substitutions, so you don't have to negotiate the service building by building.

businesses.title: Businesses and shopping centres
businesses.description: Reception and access control adapt to a business's visitor and supplier volume, not a residential building's rhythm: more traffic at peak times, parcel logging, and attending customers or staff.

security.title: CCTV and Access Control
security.summary: Design, installation and maintenance of video surveillance and access control systems for your community, building, business or shopping centre. We are not a private security firm: we do not provide guards or connect to an alarm receiving centre.
security.description: We design the security system around the actual access points of each community, building, business or shopping centre, install it, and maintain it so cameras and access controls are still working the day they're actually needed.
security.cta: Request a security assessment for my building or business

subservices.title: Video surveillance (CCTV)
subservices.description: Cameras go where the building actually has blind spots (entrances, garage, common areas), not in a standard pattern. Recordings are deleted within one month of being captured, as article 22.3 of the Spanish data protection act requires, unless they record events that must be evidenced before the competent authority. The data controller is the community or the company that owns the installation; we maintain it on their behalf and follow their instructions.

subservices.title: Electronic access control
subservices.description: Each card or code is tied to a specific home and, if the community asks, to a specific time window. For example, to let an external cleaning crew in only during their contracted hours, with no one needing to open the door for them.

subservices.title: Equipment maintenance
subservices.description: We check the condition of cameras and recorders according to the maintenance plan contracted — quarterly by default — and replace recording drives before they fail through wear. The point is to catch the problem before the community realises it has gone weeks without recording.

subservices.title: Technical fault support
subservices.description: A technician reviews the report within 24 working hours. If the fault takes a critical element out of service, such as a downed access camera or a door that won't lock, the repair becomes a priority.

faq.question: How long is footage kept?
faq.answer: Yes. The installation is signposted, camera placement avoids public streets and private spaces, and retention follows article 22.3 of the Spanish data protection act. The data controller remains the community, who must inform residents and handle their rights; we act as processor.

faq.question: Who can view the recordings?
faq.answer: Only staff authorised by the community, usually the president and the property administrator, with restricted, logged access.

faq.question: Can the system be expanded later?
faq.answer: Yes, the project is designed so cameras or access-control points can be added later without replacing the whole system.

faq.question: What happens if a camera stops working?
faq.answer: It's treated as a priority fault, not routine maintenance: a technician reviews the equipment issue within 24 working hours.

faq.question: How much does it cost to install CCTV in a community?
faq.answer: It depends on the number of entry points, cameras and the type of access control installed. We design the project around each building's real entry points and prepare a fixed quote.

faq.question: How are access cards or codes assigned?
faq.answer: Each card or code is tied to a specific home and, if the community asks, to a specific time window — for example, to limit external staff access to their contracted hours.

faq.question: How often are cameras and recorders checked?
faq.answer: At whatever frequency is set in the maintenance contract; quarterly by default, replacing recording drives before they fail through wear, so the problem is caught before the community notices it has gone weeks without recording.

faq.question: Do the cameras comply with data protection law?
faq.answer: Yes. The installation is signposted, camera positioning avoids public streets and private spaces, and retention follows article 22.3 of the LOPDGDD. The community remains the data controller, and it is their job to inform residents and handle their rights requests; we act as processor.

pools.title: Pool maintenance
pools.summary: Full pool service for homeowner communities, buildings and complexes with a swimming area: water maintenance throughout the season, season opening and closing, and a qualified lifeguard at the pools where regulations require one.
pools.description: We handle the chemical maintenance and cleaning of the community pool throughout the bathing season, plus opening and closing the season. Where Comunidad de Madrid regulations require a lifeguard based on the pool's surface area or capacity, we provide one with a current qualification; where they do not, you can still hire lifeguarding separately.
pools.cta: Get my pool ready for the season

subservices.title: Water chemical maintenance
subservices.description: Real Decreto 742/2013, which sets the health criteria for collective-use pools — and a community pool is one — requires pool water to hold a pH between 7.2 and 8.0 and residual free chlorine between 0.5 and 2 mg/l. Within that range we work to a narrower target, a pH between 7.2 and 7.6, because that is where chlorine disinfects best and irritates eyes least. It is measured daily and the dose is adjusted to how much the pool is actually used, not to a fixed factory schedule.

subservices.title: Cleaning the pool and deck
subservices.description: The pool floor and walls are brushed to prevent algae, and the deck area is cleaned daily during peak season, which is when it actually gets dirty. The goal is for it to actually be clean, not just look it.

subservices.title: Qualified lifeguards, where required
subservices.description: If the pool needs a lifeguard, we provide one holding a current official aquatic lifesaving qualification, covering the full bathing schedule the community sets: no unsupervised gaps at midday or on the last weekend of the season. Who needs one is not our call — it is set by Comunidad de Madrid regulations according to the water surface area and the pool's capacity. We check it for your pool before quoting and tell you in writing.

subservices.title: Season opening and closing
subservices.description: Before opening we check pumps, filters and the dosing system, and deep-clean after winter. When closing, we cover the pool and protect the equipment from humidity and cold so it reaches next season intact.

faq.question: When does the service run, from and to?
faq.answer: Usually from June to September, but we adjust the dates to the actual opening and closing calendar the community decides on.

faq.question: Do I need a lifeguard if the pool is small?
faq.answer: Not always. It is determined by Comunidad de Madrid regulations based on the water surface area and the pool's capacity, not the type of community. We check it for your pool before quoting and tell you in writing whether it is required: if it is, it is included in the proposal; if not, you can still hire it, knowing it is the community's decision and not a legal obligation.

faq.question: What happens if the lifeguard is out for a day?
faq.answer: We cover the absence with another qualified lifeguard; where the service includes lifeguarding, the pool is never left unsupervised on any day of the contracted schedule.

faq.question: Can I hire just the chemical maintenance, without a lifeguard?
faq.answer: Yes, water maintenance and lifeguarding can be contracted separately, depending on what the community already has covered.

faq.question: How are the water's pH and chlorine controlled?
faq.answer: They are measured daily. Real Decreto 742/2013 allows a pH of 7.2 to 8.0 and residual free chlorine of 0.5 to 2 mg/l; we aim at the lower end of the pH range (7.2–7.6), where chlorine performs best, and adjust the dose to how much the pool has actually been used that day.

faq.question: What does opening and closing the season involve?
faq.answer: Before opening we check the pumps, filters and dosing system, and deep clean after the winter. At closing, we cover the pool and protect the plant from damp and cold.

faq.question: Are the lifeguards' qualifications current?
faq.answer: Yes, they all hold a current official aquatic lifesaving qualification. Where the service includes lifeguarding, we cover the full bathing schedule the community sets, with no gaps at midday or on the last weekend of the season, and absences are covered by another qualified lifeguard.

faq.question: Can the service cover a complex with several pools?
faq.answer: Yes. We size the maintenance and lifeguarding team to the number of pools and the complex's actual capacity, rather than applying a single standard plan.

cleaning.title: Cleaning for communities and buildings
cleaning.summary: Complete cleaning of common areas, windows and garages so your community, building, business or shopping centre looks its best all year round.
cleaning.description: A fixed team takes care of cleaning the entrance, stairs, common areas and garage, at whatever frequency each community, building, business or shopping centre needs.

subservices.title: Cleaning common areas
subservices.description: The team follows a task plan by area (entrance, stairs, lift) so no corner gets skipped, at whatever frequency the community, building or business decides: from daily to twice a week.

subservices.title: Window cleaning
subservices.description: Entrance and common-area windows are part of the regular plan. Accessible façade cleaning with a pole is scheduled as an add-on depending on the building's height and access, not bundled by default in every case.

subservices.title: Garage cleaning
subservices.description: Sweeping and mopping the ramp, parking spaces and aisles, with specific treatment for oil and grease stains. Scheduled at whatever frequency the community's, building's or business's car park needs.

subservices.title: Supply of materials
subservices.description: Cleaning products meet current regulations, and Imora offers eco-friendly alternatives at no extra cost if the community prefers them. The community or business never has to buy or store products.

faq.question: How often is the building cleaned?
faq.answer: Whatever the community, building or business decides: from a weekly clean to a daily team, depending on the size and use of the property.

faq.question: Does it include cleaning inside private homes or offices?
faq.answer: No, the service covers common areas only: entrance, stairs, garage and shared outdoor areas.

faq.question: Can I request a one-off clean, not a recurring one?
faq.answer: Yes, for example after building work or before a community or business event, as an add-on to the regular plan.

faq.question: Is garage cleaning included?
faq.answer: It can be included in the general plan or hired as an add-on, depending on the condition and use of the garage or car park.

faq.question: How much does cleaning a residential community cost?
faq.answer: It depends on the frequency, the size of the building and the areas covered (entrance hall, stairs, garage, glazing). We prepare a fixed quote after visiting the property.

faq.question: Can I switch cleaning company without the day-to-day being disrupted?
faq.answer: Yes. We coordinate the handover with your current property manager so the team is operating from day one with no gap in service.

faq.question: What cleaning products are used?
faq.answer: Products that comply with current regulations; we offer eco-friendly alternatives at no extra cost if the community prefers them. The community does not have to handle purchasing or storage.

faq.question: Does it include cleaning the façade or glass at height?
faq.answer: Entrance and communal-area glazing is part of the standard plan. Façade cleaning with a pole system is scheduled as an additional service, depending on the building's height and access.

communities.title: Homeowner communities
communities.description: Cleaning frequency for the entrance, stairs and garage adapts to the community's actual size, from a weekly clean to a daily team, so the community doesn't over-contract for lack of a middle-ground plan.

propertyManagers.title: Property management firms
propertyManagers.description: A single cleaning team can serve several communities in your portfolio with consistent quality standards, so you don't have to compare different providers every time a building renews its contract.

businesses.title: Businesses and shopping centres
businesses.description: Cleaning for a business or shopping centre is scheduled outside opening hours when requested, and covers areas a residential community doesn't have: shop windows, loading areas or high-traffic common spaces.

gardening.title: Gardening and green areas
gardening.summary: Design, upkeep and pruning of gardens and green areas for communities, buildings, businesses and shopping centres.
gardening.description: A gardening team experienced in communities and commercial spaces handles pruning, irrigation and the upkeep of lawns, hedges and green areas, with periodic visits or an annual plan depending on what each property or business needs.

subservices.title: Pruning and tree care
subservices.description: Pruning is planned around each plant's species and flowering season, not a fixed date for the whole garden. Pruning a tree or rose bush at the wrong time can cost you a whole year's blooms or growth.

subservices.title: Automatic irrigation and water control
subservices.description: We check and program automatic irrigation systems to match water use to the season, avoiding both plant water stress and unnecessary spending across common areas, outdoor car parks or business and shopping-centre entrances.

subservices.title: Lawns, hedges and ornamental areas
subservices.description: Mowing, hedge trimming and care of ornamental areas at whatever frequency the season sets, so the green areas of the community, building or shopping centre stay well kept all year round.

subservices.title: Green waste removal
subservices.description: Pruning, mowing and leaf waste is removed after every visit, so the garden area and vehicle or pedestrian access are never left cluttered with green waste.

faq.question: Can gardening be hired together with cleaning?
faq.answer: Yes, it can be hired together with the cleaning service or on its own, depending on what the community, building or business already has in place.

faq.question: How often is the upkeep carried out?
faq.answer: Whatever each community or business decides: from fortnightly visits to a weekly plan during peak season, when growth is highest.

faq.question: Do you service gardens for small communities as well as shopping centres or business parks?
faq.answer: Yes, we adapt the team and frequency to the real size of the green area, from a lobby garden to the outdoor areas of a shopping centre or business park.

faq.question: Does it include replacing plants that don't survive?
faq.answer: Replacing dead or damaged plants is quoted as an add-on service, since it depends on the species and the cause of the damage.

faq.question: How much does a community's gardening cost per month?
faq.answer: It depends on the size of the green area and the frequency chosen. We prepare a quote after visiting the grounds, with no hidden charges.

faq.question: How is it decided when to prune each plant?
faq.answer: Pruning is planned around each plant's species and flowering season, not on a single fixed date for the whole garden, so as not to compromise next year's flowering or growth.

faq.question: Do you check the automatic irrigation system?
faq.answer: Yes. We check and programme the automatic irrigation to match water use to the season, avoiding both water stress for the plants and unnecessary cost.

faq.question: What happens to the pruning and mowing waste?
faq.answer: It is removed after each visit, so neither the grounds nor the vehicle and pedestrian accesses are left blocked with green waste.

faq.question: How do I report a fault?
faq.answer: By phone, email, or through the building's concierge if you also have that service; the technician reviews the report within the agreed time.

faq.question: Are parts and materials included?
faq.answer: Labour is covered by the contracted plan; materials and replacement parts are quoted separately before any work starts.

faq.question: Do you handle emergencies outside office hours?
faq.answer: Yes, through the 24-hour emergency phone line for issues that can't wait until the next day.

faq.question: Can I hire just one type of maintenance, like electrics?
faq.answer: Yes, each area (plumbing, electrics, locksmithing, small works) can be contracted independently.

faq.question: What does electrical maintenance of communal areas cover?
faq.answer: We check the main electrical panel and the communal area lighting, and progressively replace old lighting with LED where asked, which shows up directly on the community's bill.

faq.question: Is a lock failure on a communal entrance an emergency?
faq.answer: Yes. It is treated as an emergency because it compromises the building's security, not as ordinary maintenance that can wait until Monday.

faq.question: Do you do small building works as well as repairs?
faq.answer: Yes — one-off masonry, painting or carpentry repairs in communal areas, the kind many property managers leave pending because they have nobody to give them to.

faq.question: Is the technical team in-house or subcontracted?
faq.answer: In-house for day-to-day maintenance, which is what lets us respond quickly to plumbing, electrical, locksmith or small building work faults. For work requiring a specific licence — gas or high-voltage installations, for example — we work with accredited specialists.
